text:
sam: Heads-up — around 07:02 UTC we saw a sharp p95/p99 token-latency spike on prod, concurrent with throughput dropping ~25%. Not obvious from dashboards yet, opening thread.

priya: seeing it too, looks like requests routed to model-x-large on gpu-pool-7 had long tail. p50 unchanged.

sam: stack traces show kernel selection fell back to legacy-matmul kernel for many long sequences. suspect kernel-routing regression from yesterday's rollout.

dan: i pulled a small sample from logs:
```
2026-03-17T07:02:15Z INFO request_id=abcd kernel=legacy-matmul selected_by=fallback score=0.02 seq_len=1024 host=gpu-7
2026-03-17T07:02:15Z INFO kvcache.eviction_count=312 host=gpu-7 pod=pod-42
2026-03-17T07:02:15Z WARN batcher.queue_delay_ms=1280 batch_size=1
```

sam: that eviction_count spike looks bad — KV cache thrash causing more cache-misses which triggers smaller batches and fallback kernel. vicious loop.

eve: iirc we changed the dynamic kernel-selector threshold to be more aggressive last week (PR #543). Could be related.

priya: also noticed traces missing for ~30% of affected requests during that window. tracing sampling rate looks fine; propagation headers present in logs though.

infra-bot: incident-created id=INC-20260317-51 severity=3 assigned=eng-runtime

sam: dashboard note — token-latency chart (instrumented at post-token) shows spike, but request-latency (nginx) chart only small bump. mismatch suggests some instrumentation gap or sampling bias in token-level metrics.

dan: i ran flamegraphs on a replay of a captured request with seq_len=1024. Legacy-matmul shows ~60% CPU and slow GEMM path; new kernel is ~3x faster.

priya: can we confirm the kernel-selector log shows why fallback happened? maybe missing optimized-kernel binary on that host?

sam: searching build-up: hosts in pool had recent disk-clean job that removed /opt/kernels/tmp. logs show failure to load optimized-kernel for model-x-large due to missing shared object.

priya: so root cause could be: disk-clean removed kernel artifact -> selector falls back -> kvcache thrashes -> batches shrink -> tail latency spikes. Also traces missing because trace sampler relies on per-pod sidecar which restarted during disk-clean window.

dan: reproducer script snippet i used to profile:
```
# emulate request
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.prod/models/x-large/predict -d '@payload.json' | jq .
# record kernel selection logs
kubectl logs pod-42 -c runtime | grep kernel
```

eve: quick mitigation options: 1) restore optimized-kernel artifact to pool; 2) temporarily pin kernel-selector to prefer optimized-kernel if present; 3) bump kvcache size/disable eviction for this pool.

sam: doing emergency rollback of disk-clean job to restore /opt/kernels on gpu-pool-7 now. will also toggle selector to be conservative.

infra-bot: deploy rollback started: job/disk-clean rollback -> 07:08 UTC

priya: for observability gaps: tracing sidecar restart caused missing spans. we should increase trace sampling / instrument fallback path to emit span if sidecar down. Also dashboard mismatch: token metrics are emitted by runtime inner loop and were being sampled at 1/100 for storage. when load spikes sampling suppressed, so we lost signal.

sam: logged quick patch to emitter to emit aggregated token p95 as a dedicated metric (un-sampled) for production. PR #599.

dan: after artifact restore, kernel selection switched back around 07:12 and p95 dropped to baseline within 3 minutes. throughput recovered.

eve: follow-ups:
- add health-check for kernel artifact presence on pod start (probe failure if /opt/kernels missing)
- make disk-clean job exclude kernel dirs or run with validation step
- increase trace retention/sampling for critical paths and add fallback span emission
- adjust kvcache eviction policy to avoid immediate thrash when a bunch of cache-misses occur
- add alert for sudden divergence between token-level latency and request-level latency

priya: i'll open tickets for each and own the tracing one.

sam: thanks — documented timeline and linked logs in INC-20260317-51. assigning follow-ups. closing thread when tickets created. :thumbsup:
